name: Davanagere
headline: Selected for a UNICEF child-labour rehabilitation pilot; SSLC results have been volatile.
summary: Davanagere was chosen for a UNICEF pilot to rehabilitate child labourers, with hostels and schools built to bring them back into class, and the Chief Minister has warned teachers over results. Authorities also investigated a protocol breach at an SSLC evaluation centre.

reasons.detail: UNICEF picked the district for a child-labour rehabilitation project, building hostels and schools to reintegrate children.
The Chief Minister warned local teachers to improve results, and an SSLC evaluation-centre breach was probed.

Officials said 194 child marriages were stopped in 2023 and 25 of 26 reported cases in April-May 2024, citing poverty, superstition, tradition and low awareness. Schooling status of the girls was not reported.

A 2016 Samajika Parivarthana Janandolana and CRY study across six districts including Davangere found most young brides interviewed had left at Class 10 and many faced distance barriers. Not Davanagere-specific and dated.
About one in three candidates did not pass SSLC in 2025 (66.09 percent, 21st in the state). Exam failure is a typical exit point, but no source links it to Davanagere dropout directly.

headlines.takeaway: Six-district study including Davangere found most young brides left school at Class 10 and many faced high-school distance barriers.

responses.text: A UNICEF project funds hostels and schools to rehabilitate child labourers.
District committees of ASHA workers, Anganwadi teachers and panchayat staff monitor child marriage; a toll-free line lets children report cases and awareness drives run in schools and villages.
